title: Impact of stressors and protective factors on suicidality in gender-incongruent individuals
summary:
Background:  Suicidality is a major health concern. International studies suggest that gender-incongruent individuals are more often affected by suicidal thoughts and suicidal behavior than cisgender individuals. Possible contributing factors include discrimination, social exclusion, psychological distress, and barriers to healthcare. At the same time, social support, resilience, and good access to healthcare may have protective effects.
Research question:  This study examines whether the level of suicidality differs between three groups: gender-incongruent individuals, cisgender individuals with mental disorders, and subjectively healthy cisgender individuals. In addition, the study explores which stress-related and protective factors are associated with suicidality and whether these associations differ between the groups.
Methods: A multicenter cross-sectional observational study is planned with approximately 600 adult participants. Data will be collected anonymously using a standardized online questionnaire available in German and English. The survey assesses sociodemographic information, suicidality, and a range of stress-related and protective factors, such as social support, resilience, self-esteem, experiences of stigma and discrimination, and access to healthcare.
